R101.note: Reordering the spread closes the ownerId/_id override, but caller-supplied operator objects (e.g. a top-level $where or operator values on other fields) still reach Order.findOne unsanitized - mongoose.sanitizeFilter() or a scalar check is the appropriate mechanism for this sink; no behaviour change for legitimate callers.

R102.note: path.join plus the path.relative containment check closes traversal, but the added ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ allowlist rejects names with a dot (e.g. reporting.js or report.v2) that the original require('./plugins/' + name) accepted, and the contract does not call for that restriction.

R103.note: POST plus [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] is the right fix, but the existing confirmation-page link now gets a 405 until the view is rewritten as a token-bearing form; the write-up states this as a required follow-up.

R104.note: Moving the uid value to a {1} filterArg gives JNDI RFC 4515 escaping and closes injection, but the not-found message now echoes the template with the literal {1} instead of the submitted value, an unstated output change.

R105.note: snprintf into message with a truncation check rejects oversized input with -1 and preserves the AUDIT <username>:<action> output and 0 return for inputs that fit.

R106.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param('s') parameterizes the username; the prepare-false guard and mysqli_stmt_get_result keep the return-null-on-failure contract and result shape unchanged.

R107.note: The fixed map of SQL fragments is the right shape for a ${} identifier slot, but it invents a new key vocabulary (created_at_desc etc.) and silently sorts any unrecognized value - including previously valid fragments like 'total_cents DESC' - as created_at ASC instead of rejecting it, which the write-up states but does not flag as a behaviour change.

R108.note: Using detected.ext ties the stored extension to the content-verified MIME type; the resulting change to the stored name (e.g. .jpeg becoming .jpg) is the fix itself and is stated.

R109.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES and UTF-8 at the point of HTML construction closes the sink; the write-up's claim that pre-8.1 PHP defaulted to ISO-8859-1 is wrong (UTF-8 since 5.4; 8.1 changed the default flags) but the code is correct.

R110.note: Range check against calibrationTable.size() before operator[] closes the out-of-bounds write and drops only updates that were previously undefined behaviour.

R111.note: The fullmatch dot-atom allowlist blocks the '>' + space parameter injection that putcmd's CRLF check misses, but it also rejects RFC-valid addresses the original accepted (quoted local parts, single-label domains like user@localhost, address literals) and turns them into a ValueError, a restriction the write-up states but the contract does not require.

R112.note: One $n placeholder per element with ids passed as the values array binds every id out of band; empty-array behaviour (IN () syntax error) is unchanged from the original.

R113.note: pathinfo final-extension check, getimagesize content check and a random stored name close the double-extension bypass; the loss of the original 'recognizable name' in the uploads listing is stated plainly and the contract ('restricts uploads to image files') supports the content check.

R114.note: push_back closes the write past size(), but clamping to std::min(count, fields.size()) silently truncates when count exceeds the source vector, whereas the stated contract requires rejecting or reporting that case rather than silently returning a shorter packet.
